thesis: Vistra is the largest competitive integrated retail electricity and power generation platform in the U.S., with ~44,000 MW of capacity across natural gas, nuclear, coal, solar, and battery storage serving ~5 million retail customers. The company is a direct beneficiary of the AI-driven surge in power demand: data center load growth, grid reliability concerns, and a renaissance in baseload power economics are tightening power markets and lifting forward prices in its core ERCOT and PJM footprints. Q2 2026 ongoing operations adjusted EBITDA rose 31% YoY to $1.77B, and management reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $6.8B–$7.6B with a 2027 midpoint opportunity of $7.4B–$7.8B. The balance sheet is leveraged (D/E ~373%, net debt ~$19.5B) and the stock is not cheap on book value, but a 13.2x forward P/E, a 0.4x PEG, and a ~$217 analyst consensus target support a BUY rating for investors comfortable with utility-style leverage and regulatory exposure.

drivers: AI power demand accelerates faster than grid planners expect, lifting ERCOT and PJM forward power prices and capacity values
PJM capacity market reforms and IRAS resolution firm new-build economics for Vistra's existing and development fleet
Cogentrix gas-generation acquisition closes and layers in accretive EBITDA and data-center-adjacent capacity
Meta and other long-term PPAs ramp, de-risking future cash flows and supporting valuation multiple expansion
Free cash flow funds continued buybacks and deleveraging, reducing the leverage premium and rerating the stock toward large-cap IPP peers

base_case.assumptions: Vistra executes against 2026–2027 EBITDA guidance at or near the midpoint, converts EBITDA to FCF, and returns capital via buybacks while modestly deleveraging. Forward P/E stays in the 13–15x range, supported by durable power demand and a constructive but not euphoric ERCOT/PJM price environment. The ~$217 analyst consensus target is consistent with this case.

risks: ERCOT interconnection queue audit or transmission constraints materially delay new data center load and suppress forward power prices
PJM regulatory uncertainty (IRAS, RBP appeals, capacity market changes) undermines new-build returns and existing asset valuations
Natural gas prices collapse or a recession cuts power demand, shrinking EBITDA and FCF and forcing deleveraging over buybacks
High leverage becomes a constraint: refinancing costs rise and the balance sheet limits financial flexibility
Competition from tech-owned energy projects and subsidized renewables/capture squeezes dispatch margins

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings (Nov 5, 2026) — consensus EPS $2.86 on revenue $7.58B; update on ERCOT/PJM pricing, hedges, and Helix progress
Helix Digital Infrastructure ramp with KKR, NVIDIA, and Kuwait Investment Authority; up to $1.0B committed for integrated power + data center infrastructure
Pending Cogentrix acquisition expected to close, adding gas-generation assets and incremental EBITDA
Long-term PPAs with hyperscalers (including Meta) ratchet and new data center power contracts are announced
Remaining ~$1.2B share repurchase authorization expected to be completed; board may add more

key_risks: High leverage — D/E ~373% and negative tangible book value make Vistra sensitive to refinancing costs and downturns
ERCOT / Texas regulatory risk — data center interconnection queue audit and potential delays to load growth
PJM regulatory uncertainty — IRAS proposal, capacity market changes, and RBP/appeals could impact asset economics
Natural gas and power price volatility — forward curves and hedge marks create GAAP noise and can compress margins
Competition from tech-owned energy projects, renewables, and battery storage
Utility/IPPs are capital-intensive and carry environmental, safety, and relicensing obligations
